detail.boundaries: There is no sharp boundary. Re = 1 is the conventional marker for where viscous forces dominate inertial ones and Re ~ 1000 for where inertia dominates; between them both matter and neither limit applies. The scallop theorem is a statement about the STOKES limit (Re -> 0), and applying it at Re = 0.9 rather than Re = 0.001 is a judgement, so the check reports the number and says how far into the limit the design actually is.

checks.reading: Re runs from 51.356 to 171.185 across the stated ranges: intermediate (neither limit applies) at one end, intermediate (neither limit applies) at the other.

checks.label: Does the air hold it up?
checks.limiting_factor: no lift coefficient: a steady maximum lift coefficient is the WRONG QUANTITY for Drosophila melanogaster, which the NCBI taxonomy places inside Insecta. This is a decision, not a missing measurement: NOT a missing measurement. A steady maximum lift coefficient is the wrong quantity for a flapping insect wing, and adding one would answer the question with a model its own source says does not apply. Dickinson, Lehmann and Sane measured forces on a dynamically scaled robotic Drosophila melanogaster wing and reported that the enhanced aerodynamic performance of insects comes from three interacting mechanisms -- delayed stall during the translational phase, and rotational circulation and wake capture during stroke reversals. The second and third exist only because the wing rotates and reverses, and a steady coefficient represents neither. Using one here would compute a lift that omits a large part of where an insect's lift actually comes from, and present the shortfall as a property of the animal. A right answer needs a quasi-steady model with translational, rotational and added-mass terms, and the wing kinematics to drive it; or a measured force trace through the wingbeat, which is what the robotic-wing experiments produce; either way a stroke amplitude, a wingbeat frequency and an angle-of-attack schedule, none of which this repository holds for any insect. Source: Dickinson MH, Lehmann FO, Sane SP 1999, Wing rotation and the aerodynamic basis of insect flight, Science 284(5422):1954-1960 (doi 10.1126/science.284.5422.1954).

what_this_layer_cannot_say: whether the organism can generate the forces its gait requires: there is no muscle model and no actuator model
whether it can pay for the motion: no metabolic rate, no cost of transport, no energy budget
whether it can control the motion or stay the right way up: no stability model
whether the gait is one a nervous system could produce or a developmental program could build

result.scope: How a design moves, as distinct from what it is made of. One theorem (the scallop theorem, which can declare a design impossible), arithmetic over declared quantities, and empirical regime indicators that are reported and never fail anything. It models no muscle, no metabolism, no control and no energy budget: a design this layer does not contradict has not been shown to move, only shown not to be self-contradictory in the ways this layer can see.
